headline: McKesson confirmed a breach potentially exposing 284 million patient records as criminals bent AI tools into weapons—hijacking Claude sessions and driving the Cursor coding assistant to break into networks.

emerging_trends.text: Criminals treated AI platforms as both prize and tool, lifting active Claude login sessions with commodity infostealers while Aurora ransomware operators drove the Cursor coding assistant into victim networks.
Extortion crews kept squeezing large enterprises, with ShinyHunters claiming 284 million records from McKesson and setting a payment deadline that pushed the distributor to confirm the breach.
emerging_trends.topic_title: McKesson Confirms Breach of 284 Million Records

emerging_trends.text: Financially motivated fraud spanned code and cash, as an attacker drained tens of millions from Tectonic on the Cronos blockchain and prosecutors extracted guilty pleas in an ATM jackpotting ring.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Attackers Drain $74 Million From Tectonic on Cronos

topics.title: McKesson Confirms Breach of 284 Million Records
topics.latest_developments: McKesson confirmed the intrusion in an SEC filing, dated its detection to August 25, 2026, and warned customers of service degradation as the ShinyHunters extortion deadline approaches.
topics.summary: McKesson, the largest US distributor of pharmaceuticals and medical supplies, said attackers reached data through an unnamed third-party application; the ShinyHunters extortion group claims 284 million records and has set a payment deadline.

sources.title: McKesson Confirms Data Breach as Attacker Deadline Looms
Pharmaceutical giant McKesson warns of 'service degradation' following cyberattack
ShinyHunters claims it stole 284 million patient records from McKesson

topics.title: Infostealers Hijack Claude Account Sessions
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic named the infostealers involved—Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine, and Acreed on Windows, plus Atomic Stealer on a few Macs—and began forcing logouts and stripping stored payment data to block unauthorized Claude usage.
topics.summary: A threat actor used commodity infostealers, which arrive with pirated software and cracks, to lift active Claude login sessions and seize accounts belonging to an unknown number of users.

sources.title: Anthropic Users Hit by Infostealer Attacks, Session Thefts
Anthropic Warns Claude Users of Infostealer Malware Infections
Anthropic locks out Claude users after infostealers hijack login sessions

topics.title: Fresh Critical Flaws in Rails, Kaspersky, and ATM Software
topics.latest_developments: The KindaRails2Shell arbitrary-file-read flaw in Ruby on Rails drew active exploitation attempts, Kaspersky patched the HardBreacher exploit that the Nightmare Eclipse toolkit fires at its Endpoint Security product, and Wired detailed nine vulnerabilities in ATM encryption and authentication software.
topics.summary: The flaws span web frameworks, endpoint security products, and cash machines, letting attackers read secrets and execute code remotely; Rails and Kaspersky have shipped patches while the ATM research exposes broader software supply-chain weakness.

sources.title: Critical Ruby on Rails Vulnerability in Attackers' Crosshairs
Nightmare Eclipse Drops 'HardBreacher' Kaspersky Product Exploit
ATM Flaws Reveal Key Weaknesses in the Software Supply Chain

topics.title: Prosecutors Move on ATM Jackpotting and Sextortion Crews
topics.latest_developments: Five Venezuelan nationals pleaded guilty in a Kansas federal ATM jackpotting case, and two Nigerian men extradited to the US faced charges over sextortion schemes tied to the deaths of two minors in Mississippi and North Carolina.
topics.summary: US prosecutors pressed financially and sexually motivated cybercrime cases; separately, researchers Erin West and Paul Raffile traveled to Nigeria and tracked a scammer to his doorstep.

sources.title: Five plead guilty in latest federal ATM jackpotting case
Nigerians extradited to US for sextortion, deaths of two teens
How Cyber Sleuths Tracked a Nigerian Scammer to His Doorstep

topics.title: Attackers Drain $74 Million From Tectonic on Cronos
topics.latest_developments: An attacker manipulated the price of the Tonic token over the weekend to borrow $74 million from the Tectonic lending platform on the Cronos blockchain, making off with at least $6 million before Cronos halted and then restarted trading.
topics.summary: Tectonic is a decentralized lending market on the Cronos network; the price-manipulation exploit drained funds and forced the chain to pause activity before resuming.

sources.title: Cronos blockchain restarts after $74 million Tectonic exploit
Fraudsters steal $6 million from Tectonic crypto platform after inflating token price

topics.title: Aurora Ransomware Wields Cursor AI Assistant
topics.latest_developments: CloudSEK and Gambit Security found operators of Aurora ransomware, a Russian-speaking crew, driving the Cursor AI coding assistant to break into at least 10 target networks.
topics.summary: Aurora, also written Aur0ra, is an emerging ransomware operation; the two analyses grew from exposed attacker infrastructure and mark another case of criminals bending a mainstream AI coding tool to intrusion work.

sources.title: Aurora Ransomware Operators Use Cursor AI in Attacks Against 10 Targets

around_town.title: Measles Outbreak Claims Another Child
around_town.latest_developments: The Lancaster County coroner tied the death of another child to the measles outbreak on August 31 as cases keep rising across Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania's measles outbreak, centered in Lancaster County, has now killed additional residents this year, the state's first measles deaths since 1991, driven by low vaccination in the affected communities.

around_town.summary: Pittsburgh wants to place a public works facility in Schenley Park near Prospect Drive, and neighbors who use the greenspace to teach children to bike and walk are objecting.
